procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and Order dated 01.05.2023 of the High Court of Punjab & Haryana at Chandigarh in CRR No.3005 of 2013
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The Trial Court Order was assailed before the Additional Session Judge, Nuh unsuccessfully, and thereafter challenged before the High Court in Criminal Revision Petition bearing number CRR No. 3005 of 2013. The High Court partly allowed the Criminal Revision Petition, upholding the conviction but modifying the sentence imposed by the Trial Court.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The decision of the High Court of Punjab & Haryana in Criminal Revision Petition bearing number CRR No. 3005 of 2013 is assailed before the Supreme Court by the Appellant. The Supreme Court partly allowed the appeal.

decision.sentence_status: Modified. The Appellants’ sentence is reduced to the period already undergone i.e., 1 (one) month; and 3 (three) days.
directions: Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

issue.issue_text: Whether the conviction and sentence imposed on the appellant for offences under Sections 323/34 and 325/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, as modified by the High Court, should be set aside or further modified.

facts: The appellant was convicted for offences under Sections 323/34 and 325/34 of the Indian Penal Code.
The High Court had modified his sentence to three months imprisonment and a fine of Rs 5000.
The underlying incident occurred in 2010, and the trial process had spanned almost 13 years.
The appellant had already served a portion of his sentence, specifically one month and three days.
application: The Supreme Court considered the "totality of circumstances" to decide on the sentence.
The Court took into account the significant delay, noting that almost 13 years had passed since the incident in 2010.
It considered the argument that the appellant had suffered the "agony of a protracted trial."
The Court also noted the fact that the appellant had already undergone almost one-third of his sentence.
Balancing these factors, the Court concluded that the sentence should be reduced.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court upheld the appellant's conviction but modified the sentence. It reduced the term of imprisonment to the period the appellant had already served, which was one month and three days.

issue.issue_text: Whether the appellant should be declared a juvenile at the time of the commission of the offence.

facts: The appellant filed an application (I.A. No. 126067 of 2023) asking the Supreme Court to declare him a juvenile at the time the offence was committed in 2010.
Separately, the appellant's counsel argued for a sentence reduction based on the long delay of 13 years in the trial and the fact that the appellant had already served over one month of his sentence.
application: The Supreme Court considered the totality of the circumstances, especially the fact that the incident occurred in 2010 and the trial was protracted.
The Court accepted the argument for a sentence reduction and modified the appellant's sentence to the period he had already served (one month and three days).
reasoning.conclusion: Because the Court had already granted the appellant relief by reducing his sentence to the time already served, it concluded that the application to be declared a juvenile did not require any consideration. The issue was effectively made moot by the Court's decision on the sentence.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the conviction and sentence imposed on the appellant for offences under Sections 323/34 and 325/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, as modified by the High Court, should be set aside or further modified.
appellant_arguments: The sentence should be reduced to the period already undergone.
The appellant has already served almost one-third of his sentence (1 month and 3 days).
The offence occurred in 2010, and the appellant has suffered through a protracted trial spanning 13 years.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the appellant should be declared a juvenile at the time of the commission of the offence.
appellant_arguments: The appellant filed an application seeking a declaration that he was a juvenile at the time of the offence.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: In exercising its sentencing discretion, a court may reduce a sentence to the period already undergone by considering the totality of the circumstances, which includes the significant passage of time since the underlying incident and the portion of the sentence already served.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The Court concluded that while the appellant's conviction was sound, the sentence should be reduced to the period already served. This decision was based on the totality of the circumstances, with a specific emphasis on the significant amount of time that had passed since the offence was committed in 2010. Consequently, the Court deemed it unnecessary to rule on the appellant's application to be declared a juvenile, as the primary relief regarding the sentence had already been granted.
legal_tests_applied: Taking into consideration the totality of circumstances
why_appellant_lost: The application seeking a declaration of juvenility was not considered because the court had already granted relief by modifying the sentence, rendering the application unnecessary. The text does not provide a reason for why the underlying conviction was upheld.
why_respondent_won: The appellant's conviction for the offences under Sections 323/34 and 325/34 of the IPC was upheld. The text does not provide the court's reasoning for upholding the conviction, only the outcome.
policy_considerations: The Court considered the significant delay in the judicial process as a mitigating factor in sentencing, noting that the "underlying incident occurred in 2010."
